stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: Build a rectifier + filter chain. Drag a rectifier (single diode or bridge) into the top slot, and either a capacitor or a bypass wire into the parallel branch. Watch $u_{out}(t)$ on the scope. Advance once you have seen BOTH a rippling unfiltered output AND a smoothed one.
stages.concept: A diode blocks the negative half of an AC signal. A bridge of four diodes flips the negative half instead of blocking it, doubling the ripple frequency. A capacitor in parallel with the load $R$ smooths the pulsed output — it charges up on each peak and discharges slowly through $R$ between peaks.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Reach both target readings. Target A demands smooth DC ($U_{ripple}$ tiny). Target B demands the raw unfiltered pulse ($U_{avg}$ low, ripple huge). Both must be hit in the same run.
stages.concept: Full-wave rectification uses the whole AC cycle, so ripple frequency is $2f = 100\,\text{Hz}$ (not $50\,\text{Hz}$) and the smoothed average is nearly the peak $U_{max}$. For a filter cap: $\Delta U \approx U_{max} / (f_{r} R C)$, where $f_r$ = ripple frequency.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: The filter branch is pre-set. Look at $U_{max}$, $R$, $C$ and the target readouts. Compute on paper which rectifier (half-wave or bridge) gives that $U_{avg}$ and $U_{ripple}$, then place it in the empty slot. One attempt — a wrong pick rotates to a new scenario.
stages.concept: For a bridge + filter cap: $U_{avg} \approx U_{max} - 2 V_D - \Delta U / 2$ and $\Delta U \approx (U_{max} - 2 V_D) / (2 f R C)$. For a half-wave + filter cap: same formulas but with $V_D$ instead of $2 V_D$ and $f$ instead of $2 f$. Unfiltered half-wave: $U_{avg} = (U_{max} - V_D) / \pi$.

labels.stage3_place: choose a rectifier from the palette
labels.stage3_wrong: wrong — the ripple frequency doesn't match. New scenario…
labels.diag_empty: place a component in each highlighted slot
labels.diag_ac_only: no rectifier — output is still AC
labels.tip1: drag from the palette to the two dashed slots; drag out to remove; try each of the four combinations
labels.tip2: hit target A with bridge + capacitor, target B with a single diode and no cap — swap between them
labels.tip3: which rectifier makes the ripple match the target?
labels.peek_tip: Ripple frequency identifies the rectifier: 50 Hz means half-wave, 100 Hz means bridge. With a filter cap, ΔU ≈ U_max/(f_r·R·C) — bridge doubles f_r and halves ΔU.

1.1: The right palette holds four items. Drop one rectifier in the top slot, one filter choice in the vertical slot.
1.2: First try single diode + bypass wire: you'll see half of the AC wave, once every 20 ms.
1.3: Then swap the wire for a capacitor: the scope trace flattens into near-DC. Both states are required to advance.

2.1: Target A wants near-flat DC — only the smoothest configuration reaches it.
2.2: Target B wants an unfiltered half-wave hump: pulses at 50 Hz, high ripple, low average.
2.3: You don't need to hit both at once — reach A with one config, then rebuild for B.

3.1: Read $U_{max}$, $R$, and $C$ from the schematic. The filter branch is fixed.
3.2: If the filter is a capacitor, compare $U_{avg}$ near $U_{max}$ (bridge, low $\Delta U$) vs about $U_{max} - \Delta U_{half}/2$ (half-wave, twice the ripple).
3.3: If the filter is bypassed, the average is $(U_{max}-V_D)/\pi$ for half-wave, $2(U_{max}-2V_D)/\pi$ for bridge — the bridge doubles the average.
